I am a 50-year-old woman in Quzhou County, and I never went to school. I cannot read the numbers on the fertilizer bags very well, but I know my land by touch and by memory. My family has about 8 mu of flat land. Every year I grow winter wheat and summer corn — that is what everyone in my village does, and it is the only way I know to make sure we have enough to eat and a little cash to spare. I thought about planting cotton, but my back is not what it used to be, and cotton needs too much hand-picking. Wheat and corn are safer.

For the wheat, I will rotary-till the field in early October and sow about 30 jin of improved seed per mu. I save some seed from last year and buy the rest from the village supply store. I will put down one big bag of compound fertilizer as a base, and half a bag of urea at green-up time when the wheat looks yellow. I will irrigate three times: once in winter, once at jointing, and once at grain filling. I will spray herbicide once after sowing, and if the aphids come, I will spray insecticide one more time. I hope to get around 450 kg per mu.

For the corn, I plant it right after the wheat comes off in mid-June. There is no time to plough — barely a week — so I use no-tillage planting with the machine. I buy hybrid seed, about one small package per mu. I put down one bag of compound fertilizer when planting. I will irrigate twice if the rain does not come: once when the seedlings are small, and once when the stalks are tall. Two sprays for weeds and bugs should be enough. I expect about 500 kg per mu if the weather holds.

I do not calculate anything. I just do what worked last year. If I cut back on fertilizer, the yield drops, and I cannot afford a bad year.
